SELECT 
    hp.value / 1000.0 AS "Pressure (kPa)"
FROM gman_sinf22.historical_production hp
WHERE hp.sensor_id = 3
ORDER BY hp.date DESC 
LIMIT 1;

SELECT 
  DATE_TRUNC('minute', hp.date) AS time, 
  AVG(CASE WHEN hp.sensor_id = 3 THEN hp.value END) AS "Average Pressure (Pa)",
  AVG(CASE WHEN hp.sensor_id = 4 THEN hp.value END) AS "Average Flow (m³/s)"
FROM gman_sinf22.historical_production hp
WHERE hp.sensor_id IN (3, 4)
GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('minute', hp.date) 
ORDER BY time ASC;

WITH max_date AS (
    SELECT MAX(date) AS last_now FROM gman_sinf22.historical_production
)
SELECT 
    DATE_TRUNC('minute', hp.date) AS time, 
    AVG(hp.value) AS "Power (kW)"
FROM gman_sinf22.historical_production hp
CROSS JOIN max_date md
WHERE hp.sensor_id = 2
  AND hp.date >= md.last_now - INTERVAL '1 hour'
GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('minute', hp.date)
ORDER BY time ASC;

WITH max_date AS (
    SELECT MAX(date) AS last_now FROM gman_sinf22.historical_production
),
stats AS (
    SELECT
        hp.sensor_id,
        hp.date,
        hp.value,
        AVG(hp.value) OVER (PARTITION BY hp.sensor_id) AS avg_val,
        STDDEV(hp.value) OVER (PARTITION BY hp.sensor_id) AS std_val
    FROM gman_sinf22.historical_production hp
    JOIN gman_sinf22.sensor se ON se.sensor_id = hp.sensor_id
    CROSS JOIN max_date md
    WHERE se.station_id = 1
      AND hp.date >= md.last_now - INTERVAL '24 hours'
),
last_hour AS (
    SELECT *
    FROM stats
    CROSS JOIN max_date md
    WHERE stats.date >= md.last_now - INTERVAL '1 hour'
      AND std_val > 0
)
SELECT
    -- Alterado de 3 para 2 aqui:
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ABS(value - avg_val) > (2 * std_val)) AS "Anomalous Readings",
    COUNT(*) AS "Total Readings",
    ROUND(
        100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ABS(value - avg_val) > (2 * std_val)) -- E alterado para 2 aqui também
        / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0),
    2) AS "Anomaly Rate (%)"
FROM last_hour;

SELECT 
    h.date AS "time",
    h.sensor_id AS "Sensor ID",
    s.type AS "Sensor Type",
    h.value AS "Current Value",
    s.min_value AS "Min Limit",
    s.max_value AS "Max Limit",
    s.iso_units AS "Unit"
FROM 
    "gman_sinf22"."historical_production" h
INNER JOIN 
    "gman_sinf22"."sensor" s ON h.sensor_id = s.sensor_id
INNER JOIN
    "gman_sinf22"."station" st ON s.station_id = st.station_id
WHERE 
    $__timeFilter(h.date) 
AND (h.value < s.min_value OR h.value > s.max_value)
AND st.station_id = 2
ORDER BY 
    h.date DESC;

SELECT
  date AS time,
  value
FROM gman_sinf22.historical_production 
WHERE sensor_id = 7
ORDER BY date DESC
LIMIT 1;

SELECT
  -- 1. Groups data into 1-minute averages for a smooth trend line
  date_trunc('minute', hp.date) AS "time",
  -- 2. Extracts the temperature values
  AVG(hp.value) AS "Temperature",
  -- 3. Standard metric label
  'Station 5 Cell Temperature' AS "metric"
FROM 
  gman_sinf22.historical_production as hp
JOIN 
  gman_sinf22.sensor as s ON hp.sensor_id = s.sensor_id
JOIN 
  gman_sinf22.station as st ON s.station_id = st.station_id
WHERE
  st.type ILIKE '%sorting%'               
  AND s.type ILIKE '%temperature%'
  -- Pure Postgres Time Filter using Grafana's raw millisecond variables
  AND hp.date >= TO_TIMESTAMP(${__from} / 1000.0)
  AND hp.date <= TO_TIMESTAMP(${__to} / 1000.0)
GROUP BY 
  1
ORDER BY 
  1 ASC;

SELECT
  -- 1. Groups data into 1-minute averages for a smooth trend line
  date_trunc('minute', hp.date) AS "time",
  -- 2. Extracts the temperature values
  AVG(hp.value) AS "Vibration",
  -- 3. Standard metric label
  'Station 5 Cell Vibration' AS "metric"
FROM 
  gman_sinf22.Historical_Production as hp
JOIN

JOIN 
  gman_sinf22.station as st ON s.station_id = st.station_id
WHERE

  -- Pure Postgres Time Filter using Grafana's raw millisecond variables
  AND hp.date >= TO_TIMESTAMP(${__from} / 1000.0)

SELECT

  AND hp.date >= TO_TIMESTAMP(${__from} / 1000.0)
  AND hp.date <= TO_TIMESTAMP(${__to} / 1000.0)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1 ASC;

SELECT
  hp.date AS "time",
  hp.value AS "Ambient Light Level"
FROM

JOIN 
  gman_sinf22.sensor as s ON hp.sensor_id = s.sensor_id
JOIN

WHERE

  AND s.type ILIKE '%light%'
  -- Filters data to your dashboard time window
  AND hp.date >= TO_TIMESTAMP(${__from} / 1000.0)
  AND hp.date <= TO_TIMESTAMP(${__to} / 1000.0)
ORDER BY 
  hp.date DESC
LIMIT 1; -- Ensures we only pass the single newest data point to the Gauge

panels.description: Panel that helps track the conveyor motor's energy consumption in real-time, allowing the detection of inefficiencies or unexpected load

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  -- Group data into dynamic time buckets (e.g., every 5s, 1m) based on your dashboard zoom level
  date_trunc('minute', hp.date) AS time,  
-- Take the average energy consumption (kW) within each time bucket
  AVG(hp.value) AS "Motor Power Draw",
  -- Label the graph line cleanly in the Grafana legend
  'Station 5 Conveyor Motor' AS "metric"
FROM 
  gman_sinf22.historical_production as hp
JOIN 
  gman_sinf22.sensor as s ON hp.sensor_id = s.sensor_id
JOIN 
  gman_sinf22.station as st ON s.station_id = st.station_id
WHERE
  -- Filter for specific station and sensor types
  st.type ILIKE '%Sorting%'             
  AND s.type ILIKE '%Electrical%' 
  -- Grafana macro to only load data for the time range selected in the UI
  AND hp.date >= TO_TIMESTAMP(${__from} / 1000.0)
  AND hp.date <= TO_TIMESTAMP(${__to} / 1000.0)
GROUP BY 
  1
ORDER BY 
  1 ASC;
